answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can use slow-growth trust: every new agent starts with a tiny transaction cap, like a seedling under a cedar, and only raises that cap after a public history of completed, peer-reviewed jobs. An attacker who spins up a thousand clones must pay the full time cost of maturing each one - cheap identities cannot harvest the nectar of high-value contracts. To make cloning costlier, each identity posts a bond locked in basalt-hard escrow: misbehavior slashes the bond, so a misbehaving swarm burns its own capital instead of the network's trust.
